boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named North Portland destinations, each anchored to a nearby corridor and a specific documented activity or feature.

cards.title: University Park — lighted ball field
cards.subtitle: N Foss Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk the paved paths and use the picnic tables; the city identifies this as its only baseball and softball field with lights outside Delta Park.
cards.short_summary: A nearby park with fields, paths, and picnic tables.
cards.evidence_claim: University Park includes playgrounds, paved paths, picnic tables, and Portland Parks’ only baseball and softball field with lights outside Delta Park.
cards.access_notes: City park; observe posted rules and field-use guidance.

cards.title: Columbia Park — nature-patch paths
cards.subtitle: N Lombard Street corridor
cards.notes: Enter at Lombard and Woolsey, then follow the walking paths through the nature patch with its planted lawn, log benches, and boulders.
cards.short_summary: A 35-acre park with a documented nature patch.
cards.evidence_claim: Columbia Park and Annex has walking paths, a nature patch, sports fields, a historic cottage, and the annex directly across N Lombard Street.
cards.access_notes: Park hours listed by the city are 5:00am–midnight.

cards.title: Pier Park — choose a court or trail
cards.subtitle: N Lombard Street corridor
cards.notes: Start from the Lombard and Bruce entrance and choose among the paved and unpaved paths, sports courts, picnic areas, or the skate park.
cards.short_summary: An 85-acre city park with varied outdoor amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Pier Park has trails, picnic areas, a skate park, courts, sports fields, a splash pad, and a disc golf course.
cards.access_notes: Park hours listed by the city are 5:00am–midnight; dogs must be leashed.

cards.title: Cathedral Park — bridge-side paths
cards.subtitle: N Edison Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the paved paths and picnic areas beneath St. Johns Bridge, and look for the nature patch’s flowering gardens, log features, and basalt elements.
cards.short_summary: A riverfront park directly beneath St. Johns Bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: Cathedral Park offers paved paths, picnic tables, riverfront views, a stage, and a nature patch under St. Johns Bridge.
cards.access_notes: Park hours listed by the city are 5:00am–midnight; use designated paths and areas.

cards.title: St. Johns Library — computers and Wi‑Fi
cards.subtitle: N Charleston Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Set up a focused work stop using the library’s computers, Wi‑Fi, scanner, printers, and laptop-lending kiosk; verify the day’s hours before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A public library branch with study-supporting services.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Johns Library provides computers, Wi‑Fi, scanning, printing, and a laptop-lending kiosk at 7510 N Charleston Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Current listed hours vary by day; confirm on the library’s location page.

cards.title: St. Johns Twin Cinemas — current films
cards.subtitle: N Lombard Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the cinema’s current program before heading to 8704 N Lombard; it identifies itself as a first-run cinema, so showtimes determine the visit.
cards.short_summary: A named N Lombard venue for scheduled film screenings.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Johns Twin Cinemas is a first-run cinema located at 8704 N Lombard Street.
cards.access_notes: Check the official cinema site for current films and showtimes.

cards.title: Portsmouth Park — field time
cards.subtitle: N Stanford Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Meet at Stanford and Depauw for the playground, soccer field, or softball field, and keep plans within the city’s posted park hours.
cards.short_summary: A compact Portsmouth park with play and field space.
cards.evidence_claim: Portsmouth Park has a playground, soccer field, and softball field at N Stanford Avenue and Depauw Street.
cards.access_notes: Park hours listed by the city are 5:00am–midnight; dogs must be leashed.

cards.title: St. Johns Park — community-center stop
cards.subtitle: N Central Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the N Central Street address as a meeting point, then pair outdoor time in the park with a visit to the St. Johns Community Center on site.
cards.short_summary: A city park that contains the St. Johns Community Center.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Johns Park contains the St. Johns Community Center and is located in the St. Johns community.
cards.access_notes: Check Portland Parks for current community-center programming and park information.

cards.title: Peninsula Crossing Trail — bike or hike
cards.subtitle: N Willamette Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Use the N Willamette Boulevard end for a bike or hike outing; the city lists the route to Columbia Boulevard and identifies both trail activities.
cards.short_summary: A named North Portland trail spanning two major corridors.
cards.evidence_claim: Peninsula Crossing Trail runs from N Willamette Boulevard to Columbia Boulevard and supports biking and hiking.
cards.access_notes: Check the city’s trail closures and delays information before traveling.

cards.title: George Park — N Fessenden play space
cards.subtitle: N Fessenden Street corridor
cards.notes: Find the park between Calhoun and Burr for its playground, walking path, picnic table, and lawn; check the city project page for current work status.
cards.short_summary: A St. Johns park with a documented redevelopment project.
cards.evidence_claim: George Park is along N Fessenden Street between N Calhoun and N Burr and includes a playground, walking path, picnic table, and open lawn.
cards.access_notes: The city lists an active redevelopment project; consult its page for current conditions.
